purpose: Ceftriaxone is a powerful antibiotic used to fight serious bacterial infections in many parts of the body, including the lungs, skin, urinary tract, abdomen, and brain. It is also used to treat sexually transmitted infections like gonorrhea and to prevent infections before certain surgeries. Because it is given as an injection or IV drip, it is often used for infections that are too serious to treat with pills alone.
how_it_works: Ceftriaxone works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria, which bacteria need to survive and grow. Think of it like knocking down the walls of a fort — without that protective wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. Your immune system can then clean up the rest and help your body heal.
common_side_effects: Pain, swelling, or redness at the injection site are very common. You may also notice diarrhea, nausea, or an upset stomach. Some people get a rash or a headache. Less commonly, it can cause dizziness or changes in your lab results like liver enzymes or blood cell counts, which your doctor will monitor.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have ever had a serious allergic reaction to penicillin or any other antibiotic, because there is a small chance of a similar reaction to ceftriaxone. Seek emergency help immediately if you develop hives, swelling of your face or throat, trouble breathing, or feel faint — these are signs of a severe allergic reaction. Do not use ceftriaxone with certain calcium-containing IV fluids, especially in newborns, as this can be dangerous. Let your doctor know if you have liver or kidney problems, gallbladder disease, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the typical dose is 1 to 2 grams given once a day by injection into a muscle or through an IV drip in a vein. For some infections like gonorrhea, a single 500 mg injection may be all that is needed. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and how long you need treatment based on your specific infection. Children receive a lower dose based on their body weight.
